sections.name: File setup, DemoRun
sections.title: Purpose and imports
sections.what: Explains that this is the demo first screen with the recorded scope loaded, followed by a replay of the saved run. Brings in the tools it needs.
sections.why: The header states that no run is started and nothing is saved, which sets the limits of this file.

sections.name: useDemoRun
sections.title: Fetching the recorded run
sections.what: Asks the server for the recorded demo run once when demo mode is on, and keeps the answer.
sections.why: The recorded run does not change, so fetching it once is enough.
sections.watch_out: Because the data is kept forever, a newly saved demo run will not appear until the page is reloaded.

sections.name: demoScope
sections.title: Turning the recorded scope into a picker scope
sections.what: Converts the recorded scope into the format the scope picker uses, filling any missing lists with empty ones.
sections.why: Lets the picker show the recorded selection exactly as it was saved.
sections.watch_out: If the recorded scope is missing, the picker gets an empty selection, not the recorded projects.

sections.name: useLessonsDemoGate, fmt
sections.title: Checking the scope matches the recording
sections.what: Compares the projects on screen with the recorded cohort. It counts projects missing from the screen and projects on the screen that were not recorded, and says whether the two match exactly. It also provides the action that opens the replay page.
sections.why: A replay is only honest when the screen shows the same projects that were used in the saved result.
sections.watch_out: A match needs at least one recorded project, so an empty recording never counts as a match.

sections.name: DemoScopeNotice
sections.title: Notice shown on the start page
sections.what: Shows a loading note while fetching, an error note if the recording is unavailable, a green confirmation with hints when the scope matches, or a warning with buttons to restore the recorded selection or build a live deck.
sections.why: Tells the user whether the replay can be trusted for the scope they picked, and what to do next.
sections.watch_out: The warning shows counts of projects but not which ones differ, so a user cannot see the exact mismatch from this view.

summary: Handles the demo mode for Lessons Learnt: it fetches the recorded run for the demo and checks that the scope on screen matches that run before offering to replay it.
purpose: Lets someone see a real saved result without starting a new run and spending time or money on one.
why: The file header states the intent: nothing is started and nothing is saved. The reason for the exact-match rule is stated in a comment as a match between the displayed scope and the recorded run.
how: `useDemoRun` fetches the recorded run once and keeps it. `demoScope` turns the recorded scope into the picker's scope format. `useLessonsDemoGate` compares the projects on screen with the recorded projects and reports any missing or extra ones. `DemoScopeNotice` shows either a match message with hints, or a warning with buttons to restore the recorded selection or start a live run.
inputs: A flag that turns demo mode on, the list of project ids currently resolved from the scope, and the recorded run from the server.
outputs: A match status with counts of missing and extra projects, a notice panel, and a navigation action that opens the replay page.
risks: The match is exact. A single project added or removed will block the replay, which is intended but can confuse users. The data is cached forever, so a changed recorded run will not show until reload.
debug: If the replay is refused, compare `cohortProjectIds` from the server with the resolved project list. If the notice shows an error, check the `demo-run` endpoint response. If the recorded run is missing, check that the server has a demo run saved.
